- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment ≤ 0.3) — model is overly optimistic, fails to reflect bearish momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts toward historical mean too aggressively — especially in 30-day horizon.
- Forecast lags in downward corrections: when true price drops sharply, model takes 2–3 days to adjust, especially if sentiment was positive recently.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overweights upward momentum and fails to account for eventual pullback.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early bearish signals — especially if sentiment turns negative within 5 days of forecast window.
- If sentiment is mixed or trending sideways, model tends to average out — underestimating downside risk and overestimating upside potential.
- Overshoots in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is strong — model assumes momentum will continue, but sentiment shifts or reverses.
